title: Cuellar: Election did not change immigration laws — “the border is not open”
excerpt: Rep. Henry Cuellar said reports of migrants traveling north through Mexico after last week's election do not change U.S. immigration law, and that there is no open-border policy.
content:
Rep. Henry Cuellar said the results of last week’s election have not changed U.S. immigration laws, and that the border is not open to illegal entry.

Cuellar addressed reports of migrants traveling north through Mexico, saying the reports have raised questions about U.S. border policy.

“Let me be clear: The election results have not changed our immigration laws. The border is not open to illegal entry, and there is no open-border policy,” Cuellar said.

Cuellar said he supports strong border security and enforcing immigration laws, with a focus on criminals and individuals who pose a threat to public safety.

“At the same time, we must continue working toward practical, bipartisan immigration solutions that support our economy and communities across the nation,” he said.

Source: U.S. Congressman Henry Cuellar (Facebook), Nov. 13, 2026.
